Committed to innovation and excellence, Nians specializes in providing comprehensive analytics solutions that help clients optimize their operations, enhance marketing strategies, and make informed decisions. Our company fosters a collaborative and inclusive work environment, encouraging continuous learning and professional growth. With a focus on cutting-edge technology and industry best practices, Nians aims to be a leader in the analytics domain, delivering measurable value to our partners and stakeholders.

About The Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented and analytical Data Analyst to join our remote team. The ideal candidate will collect, analyze, and interpret data to uncover actionable insights that support business decisions, improve marketing performance, and optimize operational efficiency. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to transform complex data into meaningful reports and recommendations.

The Data Analyst will be responsible for collecting, cleaning, and analyzing data from multiple sources to identify trends and opportunities. This role requires a combination of technical expertise and business acumen to translate data into strategies that drive growth and efficiency. The successful candidate will have a passion for data storytelling, a keen eye for detail, and the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to stakeholders at all levels.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Business Analytics, or a related field.
2–5 years of experience as a Data Analyst or in a similar analytical role.

Responsibilities

Collect, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources to identify trends and opportunities.
Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations to support business and marketing decisions.
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and provide regular performance reports.
Analyze marketing campaign performance, customer behavior, and website analytics.
Collaborate with marketing, sales, product, and leadership teams to provide data-driven recommendations.
Perform statistical analysis to identify patterns, risks, and growth opportunities.
Ensure data accuracy, integrity, and consistency across reporting systems.
Automate recurring reports and improve data collection processes where possible.
Present findings and insights in a clear and actionable format to stakeholders.
Stay updated with industry trends, analytics tools, and best practices.

Benefits

Competitive salary based on experience.
Flexible remote work environment.

jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, DC Power Utilization Management
jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
Experience with statistical analytics and programming languages such as R, Python, Ruby, etc.

jobs.description:
Description

Build the proof that convinces customers to move to AWS. As a Benchmarking Program Manager, you will create and evangelize new benchmarking studies that quantify the KPI-driven benefits customers can achieve on AWS — the credible, data-backed evidence that AWS field teams and customers rely on to build the business case for cloud. You own these studies end to end, and once they scale, your work becomes the standard the field sells on. This is a rare seat with real autonomy: you will own the full study lifecycle, including the external vendor relationship, and you will shape how cloud value is measured and communicated across internal and external audiences. You will partner across teams to understand the needs of internal and external users, develop plans to scale each study's impact, and find innovative ways to apply benchmark insights to value-based business cases for cloud adoption. If you are energized by turning complex economics into clear, compelling proof points, move fluidly between analytical rigor and go-to-market storytelling, and thrive owning a program from concept through launch and scale, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to design studies and communicate the market realities of running IT applications and infrastructure in the cloud versus a traditional data center.
Develop and conduct new benchmarking studies that help customers understand the financial and operational benefits of the cloud.
Own the entire benchmarking study process and the external vendor relationship, including creating RFPs and evaluating, selecting, and managing vendors.
Develop and execute go-to-market and scaling mechanisms that put new studies in front of the field and customers.
Design and manage program impact-tracking metrics for management reporting.

A day in the life

You might start the morning reviewing preliminary data from a vendor-led benchmarking study, then jump into a working session with AWS field teams to understand which customer pain points the next study should address. After lunch you could be drafting the go-to-market narrative for a recently completed study, collaborating with marketing and sales enablement to ensure the messaging resonates. Later, you will connect with an external research vendor to align on methodology and timelines, and close out the day by updating your program dashboard so leadership has a clear view of study pipeline and impact.

About The Team

The AWS Cloud Economics Scale team builds tools, intellectual property, and methodology to help customers identify and quantify value creation opportunities at each stage of their journey to the cloud. We engage directly and collaboratively with customers and internal AWS teams to deliver cloud value expertise. The Cloud Economics Scale team helps answer the question: "What value can I expect to achieve by using AWS?"

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of program or project management experience
3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel (macros, pivots, lookups) at an advanced level

Preferred Qualifications

3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
3+ years of driving process improvements experience
Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

We provide a broad range of strategic, financial, operational, and technology-enabled consulting services to the full continuum of care, including hospitals, health systems, medical groups, academic medical centers, children’s hospitals, cancer centers, ambulatory surgery centers, investors, and payers/health plans.

Our work focuses on creating practical, tailored solutions that help clients maximize resources and achieve sustainable results. We value collaboration, integrity, and innovation, and are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment.

Job Details

Join Our Analytics Hub

Our growing Analytics Hub works with our consulting teams to deliver new insights, streamlined analysis, and world-class intelligence to the healthcare organizations we serve as clients. Combined with our consulting teams, you will be helping physician and executive leadership make informed decisions that can alter the course of their enterprises in areas such as physician alignment, mergers and acquisitions, service line planning, provider compensation, financial performance, transforming care models, patient access, managed care portfolio optimization, digital health expansion, and more. ECG uses a Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 environment, with Microsoft Power BI as ECG’s current analytics visualization platform.

Our detailed plans incorporate qualitative findings with data-driven strategic, operational, and financial considerations that enable organizations to pursue realistic change. Our consultants bridge the gap between strategic thinking and operational implementation with sensible action plans and tactical recommendations. This approach allows us to stretch our clients’ thinking while ensuring that initiatives with the broadest and deepest impact are prioritized and implementable. Our wide-ranging engagements often focus on helping our clients:

Position themselves for value-based care delivery.
Align hospitals and physician organizations.
Strengthen financial performance.
Enhance clinical programs.
Develop strategic partnerships and/or mergers.

As a senior data analyst, you will support the firm’s client delivery and business development efforts, working with consultants and senior leaders to manage large datasets, aggregate internal and external data, develop scalable models and other analyses, and support data visualization and presentation sets. In addition, the analyst will work directly with our internal support teams (IT, business development, and L&D) and associated vendors for data management and IT solutions and will assist with a range of innovative analytic opportunities. Gather and synthesize data from various sources (e.g., national surveys, proprietary research, client interviews, industries, markets).
Prepare analyses related to hospital inpatient databases and provider claims data.
Build flexible, dynamic, and scalable financial and operational models to forecast trends, preparing scenarios for consulting efforts related to delivery and business development (e.g., strategic planning, operational improvement, market assessments).

Perform complex analyses on big data, including cleaning, preparing, and interpreting.

Research, test, and implement solutions in Power BI.
Partner with various consulting units (Strategy & Enterprise Growth, Payer Strategy & Contracting, Health System Performance, and Medical Group Optimization) to gather requirements related to data analytics.
Develop, configure, and maintain interfaces to exchange data among Power BI, SQL databases, and other cloud-based applications.
Create and maintain analytical support documentation and operating procedures.
Develop new and innovative methodologies and approaches.
Contribute to internal education and learning opportunities for consultants and operations members for the Analytics Hub and analytics in general, and support education about ECG’s use cases related to analytics.
Assist the vice president of data analytics and AI in developing analytics and data strategy to support data analytics capabilities at the firm.

Qualifications

Strong knowledge of and passion for the healthcare industry
A bachelor’s degree in either computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, statistics, health information management, or a related degree that relies heavily on critical thinking, logic, and math
5+ years of experience in healthcare data analytics, including analyzing clinical, operational, financial, or population health data
Experience in healthcare consulting, healthcare technology, or working for a hospital or health system, using data to deliver actionable insights and recommendations
Strong proficiency in data analysis, reporting, dashboard development, and translating complex data into actionable business insights
Experience working with healthcare datasets such as claims, EHRs, patient outcomes, quality metrics, or value-based care programs is highly preferred

Excellent organizational skills

jobs.title: Project Manager (Talent Pool)
jobs.description:
Here at innocent, we’re on a mission to make it easier for everyone to get more fruit and veg into their bodies. We started back in 1999 and since then we’ve gone from selling a few smoothies at a music festival to becoming one of Europe’s biggest drinks companies with around 1,000 people (and the B Corp seal of approval).

It’s nice to be able to say things like that but we’re not patting ourselves on the back just yet. We want to show everyone that it’s possible to be a successful business while looking after people and the planet too, so we’re trying to get better in pretty much every way. And that’s where this job comes in.

This advert is for our Project Management talent pool. There isn’t an open role right now, but we regularly hire Project Managers at different levels and want to meet great people before we need them.

If a suitable role comes up, we’ll be in touch.

What You’ll Be Doing (depending On The Role)

The exact responsibilities will vary by role and level. That said, Project Managers at innocent typically get involved in things like:

Managing projects from idea to delivery (and occasionally celebration)
Creating clear plans, timelines and ways of working
Coordinating cross‑functional teams across marketing, supply chain, tech, finance and beyond
Tracking progress, risks, dependencies and budgets
Helping teams stay focused when priorities shift
Communicating updates in a way that makes sense to humans
Improving how we do project delivery over time

Senior Roles May Also Include

Leading complex programmes or multiple projects at once
Influencing senior stakeholders and decision‑making
Coaching or mentoring more junior Project Managers

Entry‑level Roles May Focus More On

Supporting project delivery and governance
Learning project tools, methodologies and best practice
Building confidence working with stakeholders

You’ll need

Again, this will vary depending on the role, but we’re generally looking for people who:

Enjoy organising work and bringing clarity to complexity
Communicate clearly, openly and with empathy
Are comfortable working with different teams and viewpoints
Can balance detail with the bigger picture
Take ownership and follow things through

For More Senior Roles, We’ll Also Look For

Proven experience delivering projects end‑to‑end
Confidence managing risk, ambiguity and change
Strong stakeholder management skills

What You’ll Get

A role matched to your experience, whether you’re building your foundations in project delivery or leading complex initiatives
The chance to work on meaningful, cross‑functional projects from idea through to delivery
Clear expectations around ownership, accountability and ways of working
Exposure to different teams, disciplines and stakeholders across the organisation
Opportunities to develop your project management skills, confidence and impact over time
The space to improve how projects are run, not just deliver them
Senior roles typically come with broader influence, more complexity, and responsibility for shaping delivery approaches. Entry‑level roles focus more on learning, support and building strong project fundamentals.

Good To Know

This is a Talent Pool and not tied to a current vacancy. We’ll review applications as we build our pipeline and reach out when a relevant opportunity comes up.

We want innocent to be a great place to work, so we do lots of stuff to make people feel at home and try to make sure everyone’s career is shaping up the way they want it to. There are plenty of opportunities to have a go at something new or take things further.

In exchange for helping us do business in the right way, you’ll get a solid rewards package that includes a salary (phew), private healthcare, a target-based bonus, and a bunch of other nice things like a day off on your birthday. And yes, you get free smoothies.

We also know that not all our drinkers come from the same background, or think the same – so why should we? At innocent, we want to be a great place to work where a diverse bunch of people from all backgrounds can turn up and thrive. When we hire, we want all the juice, bits, and pulp that make you who you are.

Even if you don’t think you can tick all the boxes, if the job sounds right for you, come and throw your hat in the ring.

jobs.description:
Zoox is building a full-stack autonomous mobility solution from the ground up. The System Behavior Analysis team is the front line for triage of driving events and software issues from our vehicle fleet and large-scale simulation, turning that data into engineering signal.

As the Technical Program Manager for System Behavior Analysis, you will sit in our Platform SW Integration organization and treat triage as a systems and data problem. Triage sits in the middle of a larger loop, from the fleet and simulation through engineering fixes to validation and release. You will partner with software development, software integration, QA, safety, product, vehicle operations and the Program Management Office.

In This Role, You Will

Drive triage accuracy and routing. Run the triage reviews that get defects, high-severity live-service issues and safety-critical events accurately classified and routed to the downstream teams that act on them.
Measure and improve triage health. Track throughput, misclassification, latency, backlog aging, automation coverage and regulatory-reportable issues, and use them to flag risks early and give leadership decision-ready updates.
Program-manage triage tooling and automation. Bring requirements to the dedicated tools and automation team, help sequence what gets automated, and track delivery, adoption and the capacity it frees.
Manage intake and escalation. Maintain the intake paths, escalation criteria and shared boards partner teams rely on.
Plan commitments and capacity. Turn milestones into quarterly triage commitments and forecast demand across onshore, offshore and vendor teams

Qualifications

Systems-Oriented Background: 3+ years in technical program management or engineering operations, with a systems mindset: you see a program and its hardware-software systems as connected parts, and trace how a change ripples upstream and downstream. Bachelor's in a technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Data fluency: experience writing your own queries and dashboards on high-volume issue or operational data, and a track record of using metrics to change how work runs.
Tool-builder disposition: experience building light tooling to run your own program, and partnering with engineering to automate manual work.
Stakeholder leadership and communication: proven ability to align teams without direct authority and give leadership clear, concise updates.
Structure from ambiguity: a track record of breaking a complex or ambiguous problem or goal into workstreams, milestones and owners.

Bonus Qualifications

Autonomous vehicle, robotics or other safety-critical experience, ideally with simulation, log replay or regression testing.
Experience program-managing internal tools or automation through to adoption.
Python or SQL, plus Jira and Confluence.

jobs.description:
Overview

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for all project administration including all contractual requirements, agreements with trade partners, purchase orders, and risk management. This individual also manages general work performance and quality, and overall team progress against the project plan.

Suffolk is seeking people who are bold. Curious. Innovative. Caring. Looking for the career opportunity of a lifetime. We’ll challenge and inspire you to be your very best. Here, you’ll find a place where you can act with purpose and integrity, bringing intelligence and grit to every aspect of your job. Join us for the chance to achieve your ambitions and build your legacy.

Responsibilities

Budget Updates:
Produce thorough forecast of Cost-to-Complete which drills down to identify potential exposures
Coordinate the use of Oracle with Expedition to readily identify exposures
Require the project team to track costs of field directives and back charges for forecasting purposes
Create detailed analysis of line-item exposures, particularly unit price contracts
Follow the Forecasting Calendar for on-time completion of forecasts
Teach the Standard Operating Procedures for budget updating to others
Change Order Management:
Require the project team to fully utilize Expedition to track all Proposed Change Order (PCO) items including in-scope and out-of-scope
Provide the Owner with up-to-date status reports relating to Changes
Require the project team to produce a monthly Owner Change Order (OCO) to prevent aging of PCO issues which further allows for timely closure of Changes with Subcontractors
Work to recover all legitimate GC costs relating to Owner Changes
Track the status of all Contract Allowances in Expedition and submits Change Order Requests (COR) when an over-run is likely
Require the project team to track all field directives and back charges in Expedition for timely processing on a monthly basis, i.e. composite clean-up, hoisting time, etc.
Project Close Out:
Establish an effective Close-out Plan early in the project which includes the early collection, review, and packaging of Contract close-out documents
Implement the use of the Noncompliance Reporting System
Require the team to utilize the Work list System to organize and manage the completion of phases of the work
Utilize the Completion-Compliance-Quality Form (CCQ) process for close-out
Teach close out process to other SCCI employees
Owner/Sub Requisition Process:
Require the project team to have the completed pay requisitions approved by the Owner no later than the 1st of each month
Produce an effective Schedule of Values
Establish a regimented process for the collection of payments no later than 30 days and subsequent efficient system for the payment to Subcontractors
Review the Hold Reports before payment is due to allow for timely handling of deficiency issues and payment to Subcontractors/Vendors
Cash Management:
Consistently manage the cash flow of the Project to maintain a fiscally responsible position for SCCI
Produce an effective Schedule of Values which supports a strong cash flow position
Review each Subcontractors initial Schedule of Values to prevent overpayment
Review Sub/Vendor requisitions to prevent payment of unsigned or unfunded Change Orders
Produce and update the cash model for the Owner to prevent surprises
Produce an accurate percent complete projection to support the SCCI financial management process
Meeting Management:
Establishes a meeting regiment for the Project Team which provides for effective communication and problem solving
Follow the SOP for focused meetings such as PM/PE, OAC's, subcontractor meetings, coordination meetings, Precon Sessions, etc.
Manage all meetings by agenda and work to time limits
Contract Logs:
Require the Project Team to assemble and maintain the Project Logs (Cash Management, Change Management, Noncompliance, Buy-Schedule, Contracts, Procurement, Submittals, RFI's, Safety, Hold Reports, Construction Schedule, Work lists) and periodically review for accuracy
Conduct focus meetings once per month to review the maintenance of those logs and drills down to identify potential exposures and issues
Subcontractor Relationships:
Establish a "Firm but Fair" approach to building relationships with Subcontractors
Promote an environment of organization and professionalism with Subcontractors
Address issues immediately with a non-performing Subcontractor to protect SCCI from resulting delay and potential impact
Exhibit B Purchasing Process:
Work with the Project Team, including Superintendents and Estimators, to consistently produce clear, thorough, and accurate Scopes of Work based on drilled down review of documents
Organize and administer a well-planned purchasing process to prevent the "Just in time" purchase of materials
Understand the priority of timely buy-out and gather the resources to meet the buy schedule
Schedule Management:

Develops written materials such as correspondence, educational content, and training resources.

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Position Description

The City of Rochester invites applications for

Senior Project Manager

The City of Rochester is committed to a community where all members feel a sense of belonging. We commit to recognizing the diversity of our community members, listening to ALL
voices and providing equitable services to create an inclusive place to live, play and work.

We believe EQUITY
should be at the center of all our work. We strive to represent our community in our teammates, as we know that diverse and inclusive teams are more innovative, and have an empowering impact on the work, progress and culture of our community.

It takes us all working together

Nature of Work

The Senior Project Manager leads the planning and delivery of large, complex capital improvement projects and enterprise-wide transformational initiatives that advance the City of Rochester’s strategic goals. This position manages projects through the full lifecycle—from concept and scope development through design, construction, implementation, and closeout—ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in alignment with City Council direction, organizational priorities, and community needs.

The Senior Project Manager provides advanced project management expertise, oversees consultants and contractors, coordinates work across departments, manages budgets and risk, and communicates complex technical information to diverse audiences. The position also mentors project managers and other junior project team members and contributes to continuous improvement of the City’s project and change management practices.

Work Schedule:
The regular work schedule is Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

Pay
: The 2026 h iring range for this position is $99,419 to $116,964 with advancement to $146,205

Benefits:
This position is eligible for benefits offered by the City of Rochester. Please check out the benefits tab at the top of the page for more details.

To have your application considered in the first round of reviews, please apply before October 18, 2026, at 11:59pm CST.
Applications will be accepted until the position is filled.

The City of Rochester will not sponsor or transfer visas for this position including F1 OPT STEM.

Duties And Responsibilities

The work below is representative of the scope of work performed within this job classification.

Lead the delivery of large, complex capital improvement projects from planning through closeout, ensuring high-quality outcomes that create meaningful and lasting community impact.
Manage assigned projects throughout their full life cycle including the planning phase, scope establishment, consultant procurement and contract negotiations, along with leading steps of the various phases of design, right-of-way procurement, permitting, construction bidding, construction administration, project close-out and turnover.
Develop and manage comprehensive project plans, budgets, schedules and stakeholder communications; ensuring technical requirements and contractual/legal obligations are met.
Lead and coordinate multidisciplinary project teams to deliver projects that meet scope, schedule, budget, quality, and performance expectations.
Provide technical research and analysis to evaluate, implement, and manage complex project plans and specifications concurrently to meet defined outcomes.
Collaborate with City staff to write and submit grant applications for projects that the City of Rochester pursues.
Coordinate project plans, schedules, and resources to optimize project execution and minimize disruptions to residents, businesses, and City operations.
Monitor projects and produce periodic reports to communicate project status in clear and simple terms to stakeholders.
Manage project expenses to ensure they remain within budget parameters and in compliance with internal procedures and controls.
Anticipate and identify potential issues and risks that may impact project implementation; provide quality reviews, risk analysis, and implement risk mitigation strategies.
Coordinate with internal and external partners to address and problem-solve construction-related issues or concerns.
Establish safety goals and plans for each project.
Manage construction work quality and ensure it conforms to current city policies, technical standards, and ordinances.
Serve as an owner's representative during the design and construction phases and manage consultants and contractors retained for project delivery, managing project finances, and the overall project delivery process.
Train and mentor other Project Managers.
Budget and Contract Management
Develop and manage comprehensive project budgets and funding strategies.
Manage project expenditures to ensure compliance with approved budgets, internal controls, and funding requirements.
Prepare contracts for construction of capital projects and negotiate revisions, changes and additions to construction contracts as needed to support successful project delivery.
Advocate and lead negotiations for the City during disputes, disagreements, modifications or change orders related to construction contracts or project changes.
Serve as a City representative for high visibility projects, including multimodal transportation projects, infrastructure projects, and transformational initiatives.
Oversee and serve as the primary contact for work with contractors, developers, consultants, City staff, and their representatives on projects.
Maintain positive working relationships with all stakeholders and foster project buy-in by clearly communicating project goals, benefits, and outcomes.
Implement communication and engagement strategies to ensure community involvement across all sectors of the community, while embracing a Business Forward Strategy that delivers capital projects while focusing on mitigating impacts to local businesses to the maximum extent feasible.
Represent the City at meetings and public forums, presenting complex information to residents, businesses, civic organizations, disadvantaged communities, regulatory agencies, industry groups, private partners, and other stakeholders.
Provide public notifications, updates, and responses to inquiries, complaints, and requests for information related to assigned projects.
Monitor project performance and prepare clear, concise status reports for internal and external stakeholders.
Prepare City Council documentation and present complex technical and financial information to City Council and other governing bodies.
Special Initiatives:
Collaborate with consultants to prepare bid packages that meet City standards and Women/Minority-owned Business Enterprise program goals based on contract values.
Actively work to engage, leverage, and support the City’s Women and Minority Owned Business Program.
Utilize unique and innovative strategies and practices to measure project success through the establishment of data metrics that analyze short- and long-term impacts.
Participate in the department's annual capital and operating budget preparation and monitoring throughout the year which includes personnel, equipment, technology, vehicles, and software costs.
Ensure all assigned projects meet the requirements of the Destination Medical Center District Design Guidelines and other applicable City standards.
Manage consulting contracts for special projects.

Perform Other Duties As Assigned Or Necessary.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Minimum Qualifications

Education and Experience

A Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning/Design, Construction Management, Project Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, or closely related field from an accredited four-year college or university AND a minimum of six (6) years of full-time experience being a key part of a project team that delivers complex civil infrastructure, parks, or urban design type projects

OR

An equivalent combination of education, certification and experience sufficient to successfully perform the essential duties of the position may be considered.

Licenses and/or Certifications

Valid driver's license

Desirable Qualifications

A Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning/Design, Construction Management, Project Management, Urban/Planning, Business Administration, Public Administration, or closely related field from an accredited college or university.

10-years of full-time project management experience involving capital project delivery

Experience managing large multi-discipline projects, construction services, or as an on-site Project Manager.

Project management certification

Professional licensure as a civil engineer, architect, or landscape architect

If this work interests you but you are unsure if you meet all the job requirements listed above, please apply anyway! Your experience is likely more applicable to the role than you think, and the City is interested in candidates who can bring not only technical expertise but a variety of lived experience to the team.

Additional Information

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the following represents the physical and environmental demands for this position. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions with or without accommodation.

In consideration of the overall amount of physical effort required to perform this position, the work is best described as Light Work : Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg controls requires exertion of forces greater than that for Sedentary Work and the worker sits most of the time, the job is rated for Light Work.

Physical demands

new_jobs.description:
At U.S. Bank, we’re on a journey to do our best. Helping the customers and businesses we serve to make better and smarter financial decisions and enabling the communities we support to grow and succeed. We believe it takes all of us to bring our shared ambition to life, and each person is unique in their potential. A career with U.S. Bank gives you a wide, ever-growing range of opportunities to discover what makes you thrive at every stage of your career. Try new things, learn new skills and discover what you excel at—all from Day One.

Job Description

The Data Strategy Project Manager is a hands-on, execution-focused professional who blends data strategy analysis with disciplined program management and strategic ownership-building and maintaining roadmaps, owning the development and guidance of strategy for select cross-enterprise data products, and tracking status and financials across EDO initiatives. As the Enterprise Data Office grows quickly and takes on more concurrent workstreams, this role is critical to keeping the portfolio organized, focused, and on track.

Essential Functions

The Data Strategy Project Manager reports to the Head of Data Strategy & Administration, working closely with the EDO senior leadership group (direct reports to the Chief Data Product Officer) and the extended senior leadership group (direct reports of direct reports to the CDPO) to align roadmaps, status, and budgets across the Enterprise Data Office.

Responsibilities

Roadmap & Portfolio Planning

Own and maintain integrated roadmaps across EDO workstreams, translating strategy and leadership priorities into sequenced, trackable plans.
Identify dependencies, risks, and resourcing gaps across projects, escalating issues before they threaten timelines.

Status Reporting & Governance

Own the cadence for project status reporting-collecting, synthesizing, and packaging updates from domain and workstream leads into executive-ready materials.
Run governance routines: agenda setting, documentation, and follow-ups for EDO working groups, steering committees, and leadership forums.
Maintain a single source of truth for project status, milestones, and open issues across the EDO portfolio.
Identify and escalate cross-workstream dependencies, risks, decisions, and constraints impacting delivery across the EDO portfolio

Financial & Budget Stewardship

Track financials and budgets across EDO programs, partnering with Finance on forecasting, spend tracking, and variance analysis.
Monitor vendor spend, resource allocation, and cost efficiency across data platforms and initiatives, flagging risks to leadership.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

Hold brief (10-15 minute) weekly check-ins with individual members of the EDO senior leadership group and extended senior leadership group to gather status on their workstreams and surface blockers early.
Prepare executive-ready communications, dashboards, and briefing materials that translate technical and operational detail into clear narratives.

Data Strategy & Analysis

Own the development and guidance of strategy for select cross-enterprise data products, partnering with domain and product leads to shape direction and priorities.
Support the development of enterprise data strategy deliverables, ensuring project plans and reporting remain grounded in EDO priorities and data standards.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree, or equivalent work experience
Eight to ten years of experience in project management activities

Preferred Skills/Experience

Baseline knowledge of assigned business line or functional area
Demonstrated management and leadership skills
Strong organizational and analytical skills
Working knowledge of project management
Ability to identify and resolve exceptions and to analyze data
Excellent verbal and written communication skills

Location Expectations:

This role requires working from a U.S. Bank location three (3) or more days per week.

If there’s anything we can do to accommodate a disability during any portion of the application or hiring process, please refer to our disability accommodations for applicants.

Benefits:

Our approach to benefits and total rewards considers our team members’ whole selves and what may be needed to thrive in and outside work. That's why our benefits are designed to help you and your family boost your health, protect your financial security and give you peace of mind. Our benefits include the following:

Healthcare (medical, dental, vision)
Basic term and optional term life insurance
Short-term and long-term disability
Pregnancy disability and parental leave
401(k) and employer-funded retirement plan
Paid vacation (from two to five weeks depending on salary grade and tenure)
Up to 11 paid holiday opportunities
Adoption assistance
Sick and Safe Leave accruals of one hour for every 30 worked, up to 80 hours per calendar year unless otherwise provided by law

About the team:

LinkedIn's members entrust us with their information every day and we take their security seriously. Our core value of putting our members first powers all the decisions we make, including how we manage and protect the data of our members and customers. Information Security at LinkedIn is dedicated to protecting and securing business-critical member data and company assets. We’re hiring a Staff Security Technical Program Manager to drive execution across our Production and Enterprise Security organization. You’ll own critical programs such as vulnerability management, lead cross-functional security initiatives, and establish the operating rhythm that keeps teams aligned on priorities, OKRs, milestones, and outcomes.

You’ll bring structure to complex programs, surface risks and dependencies early, drive decisions to closure, and ensure commitments don’t fall through the cracks. You’ll provide leadership with clear, accurate program status while serving as a force multiplier for engineers by removing blockers and creating clarity without adding unnecessary process.

About the role:

Job Description: Senior Program Manager – Global Information Security
Position Overview
Avancé Consulting Group is seeking an adaptable, high-impact Senior Program Manager to embed directly with Global Information Security (GIS) leadership at a premier global investment management organization.
This role serves as a strategic execution thought partner and delivery lead to a senior pillar head within the Information Security portfolio, bridging high-level security strategies with tactical execution across Global Technology and enterprise business units. Rather than managing a strictly predefined, static scope, you will operate with significant autonomy, partnering 1-on-1 with security domain leaders to unpack complex mandates, establish program structures, prioritize critical initiatives, and drive execution across distributed enterprise teams.
Four positions are currently open across four distinct Information Security functional pillars. Candidates will be aligned to one of these specific domains based on relevant technical background and delivery strengths.
________________________________________
Role Details
• Engagement Type: Contract (12-Month Engagement with high likelihood to extend)
• Target Start Date: October 15, 2026 (Immediate hiring cadence)
• Work Arrangement: Remote (East Coast / Eastern Time alignment preferred; Charlotte, NC hub)
• Operating Model: Embedded within Global Information Security (GIS) leadership under the governance and delivery frameworks of the central Enterprise Change Office (ECO).
________________________________________
Core Responsibilities
• Strategic Thought Partnership: Serve as the dedicated delivery partner to a Security Pillar Lead, translating high-level imperatives, audit remediation goals, and emerging security demands (including AI-driven governance and operational resilience) into structured, actionable program roadmaps.
• Program Delivery & Execution: Establish milestones, drive accountability, track complex cross-functional interdependencies, and manage risks across multi-disciplinary global technology teams without requiring rigid top-down project parameters.
• Cross-Functional Orchestration: Facilitate seamless alignment between Information Security pillar leads, application engineering teams, enterprise architecture, infrastructure operations, and central change management governance.
• Scope Definition & Governance: Dissect broad, ambiguous technical mandates into discrete workstreams, project plans, and measurable operational outcomes.
• Executive Visibility & Reporting: Deliver clear visibility into portfolio delivery status, resource bottlenecks, critical path milestones, and key security deliverables for executive leadership.
________________________________________
Target Pillars & Functional Scope
Candidates will be deployed into one of the following four Information Security pillars:
1. Cybersecurity Incident Management
• Domain Focus: Cyber incident preparedness, response orchestration, crisis escalation paths, and post-incident remediation.
• Core Initiatives:
o Modernize enterprise incident response playbooks and cross-functional crisis communication workflows.
o Mature tabletop exercises and cyber simulation drills across global technology and executive leadership.
o Lead post-mortem tracking, root cause analysis (RCA), and continuous control validation workstreams.
• Specialized Acumen: Working familiarity with CSIRT/SOC operating cadences, threat escalation frameworks, and NIST Incident Handling standards (NIST SP 800-61); ability to coordinate cross-functional teams (Legal, Compliance, Communications, SecOps) under time-sensitive conditions.
2. Application Security (AppSec)
• Domain Focus: Embedding proactive security governance directly into the modern software development lifecycle (SDLC) across global engineering teams.
• Core Initiatives:
o Scale developer security enablement, threat modeling workflows, and secure coding standards across product teams.
o Operationalize centralized penetration testing scheduling, vulnerability prioritization, and third-party vendor testing engagements.
o Drive the rollout and engineering adoption of SAST, DAST, SCA, and container security scanning tooling across enterprise CI/CD pipelines.
• Specialized Acumen: Deep familiarity with DevSecOps practices, secure SDLC integration, and application vulnerability remediation cadences across distributed software engineering groups.
3. Identity & Access Security (IAM / Governance)
• Domain Focus: Enterprise identity governance, privileged access management (PAM), and machine/non-human identity controls.
• Core Initiatives:
o Lead program execution around non-human identity lifecycle management (service accounts, API keys, tokens, certificate management).
o Rationalize and execute role-based access control (RBAC) cleanups, least-privilege enforcement, and privileged access workflows.
o Modernize identity governance and administration (IGA) integration across hybrid cloud and enterprise environments.
• Specialized Acumen: Working knowledge of modern IAM architectures (e.g., SailPoint, CyberArk, Okta, Active Directory/Entra ID) and access compliance audits in financial institutions.
4. Security Tooling & Infrastructure Modernization
• Domain Focus: Delivery governance across internal and vendor-provided security tools protecting enterprise infrastructure, endpoints, and cloud environments.
• Core Initiatives:
o Plan and coordinate enterprise-wide security tooling migrations, upgrades, agent rollouts, and rationalizations.
o Track vendor integration milestones, proof-of-concept (POC) evaluations, and enterprise deployment across thousands of endpoints and server instances.
o Partner with enterprise infrastructure and cloud engineering to ensure monitoring coverage and tool telemetry integration with SIEM/data lakes.
• Specialized Acumen: Technical breadth across endpoint protection (EDR/XDR), network security tooling, vulnerability scanners, and telemetry pipelines; strong vendor delivery management.
________________________________________
Qualifications & Key Competencies
• Enterprise Program Management: 7+ years of experience leading complex, large-scale technology programs or portfolios.
• Information Security Acumen: Demonstrated experience supporting cybersecurity, InfoSec, or technology risk domains aligned with at least one of the four core pillars above.
• Consultative Problem Solver: Proven ability to thrive in ambiguous, fast-moving environments; operates effectively as a hands-on strategic partner rather than a rigid checklist-driven coordinator.
• Communication & Influence: Exceptional interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills, capable of influencing senior technical leaders, engineering directors, and cross-functional business partners.
• Delivery Frameworks: Deep experience with Agile, hybrid delivery frameworks, and Enterprise Change Office / PMO standards.\
• Financial Services & Investment Management (Nice to Have):
o Prior background within Financial Services, with a strong preference for Investment Management (buy-side / asset management) or wealth management environments.
o Familiarity with the operational, audit, compliance, and regulatory landscapes typical of global financial institutions.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager - VA Digital Modernization & AI Program
new_jobs.description:
Overview

LMI is seeking a Senior Program Manager
to serve as the highly embedded, day-to-day program leader for a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) digital modernization and artificial intelligence program. This full-time role is the visible prime point of accountability for integrated execution, customer coordination, staffing, subcontractor performance, risk, schedule, quality, financial health, and partner integration.

The Senior Program Manager will lead and coach an approximately 20+ person LMI team plus an integrated subcontractor team spanning program management, human-centered design, data and analytics, clinical informatics, architecture, engineering, governance, quality assurance, change, and adoption. The program operates through an integrated delivery model that connects use-case discovery and prioritization, solution design, piloting, implementation, measurement, and continuous improvement across multiple concurrent workstreams. The Senior Program Manager will ensure these disciplines operate as one coordinated team, with clear priorities, defined accountability, strong cross-functional collaboration, and consistent focus on mission outcomes.

This role also carries an important account-growth responsibility. The Senior Program Manager is expected to build trusted VA relationships, understand evolving mission priorities, identify adjacent needs, connect those needs to LMI capabilities, and partner with market and account leadership to cultivate organic growth. The ideal candidate combines federal program management rigor with strong client presence, business acumen, subcontractor leadership, an appetite for business development, and enough technical fluency to coordinate AI, data, HCD, clinical, security, engineering, and adoption teams. Prior VA experience is highly desired.

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, homeland, healthcare, and intelligence sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

Serve as the day-to-day leader for a complex federal program, providing integrated leadership across client delivery, people, partners, financial performance, risk, quality, and strategic priorities.
Lead, coach, and develop an approximately 20+ person multidisciplinary LMI team and integrated subcontractor team, creating clear accountability while building leadership capability throughout the organization.
Establish clear expectations for performance, delivery, collaboration, and professional growth; provide regular coaching and feedback and address performance or behavioral concerns directly when needed.
Maintain visibility across multiple concurrent projects and workstreams, ensuring priorities, resources, schedules, dependencies, risks, and outcomes remain aligned with customer and program objectives.
Own program operating rhythms, integrated planning, performance reporting, action and decision tracking, escalation paths, and executive-level visibility into program health.
Manage program financial health, staffing, forecasting, utilization, and resource planning to support a portfolio of $10M or more in annualized value while maintaining strong delivery performance.
Lead subcontractor and partner integration, including performance management, resource coordination, issue resolution, accountability, and alignment with overall program objectives.
Build and sustain trusted relationships with VA executives, program leaders, technical stakeholders, and mission partners; understand emerging priorities and translate them into actionable delivery and growth strategies.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the customer by connecting mission needs with relevant capabilities, identifying opportunities to improve outcomes, and bringing forward informed recommendations rather than simply responding to stated requirements.
Contribute to the overall growth and operational strategy for the submarket under the guidance of senior leadership, helping shape priorities, investment decisions, capability positioning, staffing strategies, and approaches for expanding LMI's presence in the market.
Proactively identify and cultivate opportunities for organic growth and adjacent-market expansion, with an emphasis on supporting objectives such as increasing direct labor by approximately 10%, expanding into adjacent submarkets, and increasing the use of program past performance to support future opportunities.
Leverage strong client relationships and knowledge of the mission environment to identify emerging needs, shape potential solutions, and position LMI to provide additional value before opportunities become formal procurements.
Partner with LMI market, growth, capture, and service-line leadership on account strategy, opportunity identification, solution development, capture activities, proposals, and client presentations.
Attend relevant industry conferences, professional forums, VA/federal events, and networking activities to strengthen LMI's visibility, develop relationships across the submarket, understand emerging customer and industry priorities, and build a network of contacts that can support future growth.
Develop relationships with industry partners, technology providers, subject-matter experts, and other organizations that may strengthen LMI's ability to pursue and deliver future opportunities.
Connect customer challenges with capabilities across LMI, bringing together technical, analytical, operational, and domain expertise to develop integrated solutions and expand the broader account.
Anticipate and resolve delivery, staffing, customer, partner, financial, and operational risks before they affect program performance, escalating strategically when senior leadership engagement is needed.
Develop and deliver executive briefings, program reviews, performance assessments, recommendations, and decision materials for VA and LMI leadership.
Ensure program activities and deliverables comply with contractual requirements and applicable federal, VA, security, privacy, accessibility, quality, and LMI standards.
Continuously improve program operations, delivery processes, team effectiveness, and customer outcomes while creating sufficient delegation and leadership depth so the Senior Program Manager is driving the program rather than becoming the program's operational bottleneck.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in business, management, public administration, information systems, engineering, health administration, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
12+ years of progressive experience leading complex federal programs, portfolios, or technology-enabled transformation efforts, with demonstrated responsibility for client delivery, staffing, financial performance, risk, schedule, quality, and organizational outcomes.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams of approximately 20 or more employees, including senior staff, technical specialists, project leaders, and subcontractor or partner personnel.
Proven ability to serve as a senior client-facing leader and trusted advisor, building durable relationships with executive stakeholders, understanding evolving mission priorities, and translating those priorities into actionable delivery and growth strategies.
Significant experience supporting federal health, technology, digital modernization, data, or transformation programs, with the ability to operate effectively across business, clinical, operational, and technical stakeholder communities.
Demonstrated experience managing a large, complex portfolio with $10M or more in annualized value, including forecasting, staffing, utilization, financial performance, resource allocation, and executive-level program reporting.
Strong people-leadership experience, including setting clear expectations, coaching and developing employees, building future leaders, recognizing strong performance, and addressing performance or behavioral issues directly when necessary.
Demonstrated success leading in a matrixed, multi-partner environment, including subcontractor management, partner coordination, cross-functional delivery, issue resolution, and accountability for integrated outcomes.
Strong executive communication and facilitation skills, including the ability to lead senior-level discussions, influence decisions, navigate difficult conversations, present recommendations, and communicate complex issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated business acumen and experience identifying opportunities to improve program performance, expand client value, and strengthen long-term account positioning.
Experience contributing to organic growth, capture, account strategy, pipeline development, or solution shaping, including identifying emerging customer needs and connecting those needs to organizational capabilities.
Ability to operate with significant independence, bring structure to ambiguity, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and balance immediate delivery requirements with longer-term strategic priorities.
Working knowledge of digital modernization, data and analytics, artificial intelligence, human-centered design, Agile delivery, cloud or low-code technologies, or related emerging technology environments sufficient to lead integrated technical and mission teams.
Ability to satisfy VA personnel vetting and background investigation requirements applicable to assigned duties and work effectively within VA-approved remote, security, privacy, records, and data-handling environments.

Desired Qualifications

Direct Department of Veterans Affairs experience, particularly supporting VHA, VA OIT, Veterans Experience Office, Digital Health, or other VA enterprise organizations. Candidates with established knowledge of VA stakeholders, governance, mission priorities, and organizational dynamics will be especially well positioned for success.
Demonstrated experience serving as a Program Director, Senior Program Manager, Portfolio Lead, Account Lead, or comparable leader on major VA or federal health programs.
Experience leading enterprise modernization initiatives that integrate technology, business processes, clinical or operational workflows, customer experience, and organizational change.
Experience advising senior federal executives on modernization strategy, operational challenges, investment priorities, emerging technologies, or future capability development.
Demonstrated success in business development and account growth, including shaping multimillion-dollar opportunities, developing win strategies, supporting capture and proposals, cultivating executive relationships, and expanding work within existing clients.
Experience building and leveraging relationships with industry partners, technology providers, and strategic partners to strengthen delivery capabilities, expand market access, and support future opportunities.
Experience representing an organization at industry conferences, federal forums, professional associations, and networking events, with an ability to build and maintain a meaningful network across the VA and federal health submarket.
Experience with AI-enabled solutions, digital health, enterprise data and analytics, customer experience, contact-center modernization, workflow transformation, or other technology-enabled mission modernization.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Work within the Global Sales Organization (GSO) Program Management Office to lead complex, cross-functional programs that advance strategic Sales and Go-to-Market priorities.

What You'll Do

Lead complex, cross-functional Sales and GTM transformation programs end-to-end, translating strategic business priorities into clear scope, outcomes, workstreams, milestones, dependencies, resource requirements, and measurable success criteria.
Manage multiple strategic programs and interconnected workstreams simultaneously, independently driving execution from initial strategy and planning through implementation, adoption, and value realization.
Bring a strong understanding of Sales and GTM organizations, processes, and operating models, partnering across Sales Leadership, Sales/Revenue Operations, Enablement, Marketing, Channel/Partners, Product, Finance, IT, and other functions to drive business outcomes.
Establish and drive business-centric program governance and operating rhythms, including integrated program plans, executive decision forums, milestones, dependencies, RAID management, resource planning, change control, and clear accountability across workstreams.
Navigate complex and ambiguous business problems, independently assessing issues, identifying options and tradeoffs, and developing recommendations that enable senior leaders to make informed decisions.
Partner with business leaders to translate strategic objectives into measurable outcomes, KPIs, adoption measures, business cases, and ROI, ensuring programs remain focused on delivering business value rather than activity alone.
Develop a deep understanding of the seller and field experience, identifying cross-functional process, technology, organizational, and adoption dependencies that may impact execution of GTM initiatives.
Serve as the connective tissue across business and technology teams, translating business requirements into executable plans and ensuring technical solutions remain aligned to Sales/GTM objectives and intended business outcomes.
Proactively identify and manage cross-program risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and competing priorities; drive teams toward resolution and escalate decisions to executive leadership when necessary.
Drive clarity and accountability across complex stakeholder groups, ensuring business owners, workstream leads, and cross-functional partners understand their responsibilities, commitments, decisions, and required outcomes.
Build trusted relationships with VP and C-level stakeholders, effectively communicating program health, strategic decisions, risks, investment requirements, and recommendations in a concise and executive-ready manner.
Influence across organizational boundaries and drive decisions without direct authority, constructively challenging assumptions and the status quo when necessary to achieve the right business outcome.
Anticipate downstream impacts of decisions across Sales, GTM, technology, operations, and other programs, ensuring dependencies and organizational implications are identified early.
Lead executive and Steering Committee governance, including developing decision-oriented materials and ensuring leadership forums result in clear decisions, ownership, and follow-through.
Manage program investment and resource requirements in partnership with business owners and Finance, including identifying capacity needs, evaluating tradeoffs, and supporting business cases and investment decisions.

Drive continuous improvement through retrospectives, lessons learned, and program health assessments, incorporating insights into future programs and PMO standards.

12+ years of progressive program management experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation programs in large organizations.

Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect program execution to business value, investment requirements, ROI, productivity, adoption, and revenue outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to influence and communicate with VP and C-level executives, navigate competing priorities, and drive cross-functional decisions without direct authority.
Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear recommendations, decisions, and executive-ready materials.
Ability to operate effectively across business and technology teams, understanding technical dependencies and translating them into business implications and actionable plans.
Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, highly cross-functional environment with significant ambiguity, balancing strategic thinking with strong execution discipline.
AI-curious and forward-thinking, with a working knowledge of emerging AI capabilities and a strong interest in how AI can transform Sales, GTM, and program management.

Strong command of program/project management methodologies and tools (e.g., Agile, Waterfall, hybrid; Smartsheet, Asana, Jira or equivalent), with the judgment to apply the right approach to the work.
Strong analytical, organizational, facilitation, and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward proactively bringing recommendations and solutions.
Experience coaching or mentoring other Project/Program Managers and contributing to broader PMO standards and capability development.
Project/Program Management certification (PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, Scrum Master, or equivalent) required; Lean Six Sigma or process improvement experience a plus.
