new_jobs.title: AI Security Analyst
new_jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Security Analyst based in India.

This role sits at the forefront of AI security and governance, helping protect an enterprise environment as the adoption of AI tools, models, and autonomous agents accelerates. You will monitor AI activity across the organisation, investigate suspicious or unauthorised usage, and turn security telemetry into actionable findings. The position combines security operations, threat detection, data protection, identity security, and emerging AI risk management. You will contribute to controls and evidence supporting AI governance initiatives, including ISO 42001 and broader regulatory readiness. Working closely with security, identity, legal, engineering, and automation teams, you will help strengthen safeguards around rapidly evolving AI technologies. This is an opportunity to shape practical AI security processes in a collaborative, globally distributed environment.

Accountabilities

Monitor enterprise AI usage across CASB, SWG, OAuth, endpoint, DLP, and other security telemetry to identify unauthorised AI applications, browser extensions, and API-based agents.
Classify AI security findings according to risk and escalate unauthorised or potentially harmful deployments for investigation and containment.
Investigate alerts involving autonomous agents and AI-powered workflows, including anomalous tool chains, unexpected data access, credential misuse, and emerging agent-based attack patterns.
Document investigation findings and coordinate remediation with automation, identity, security operations, and engineering teams.
Monitor AI usage and DLP logs for potential sensitive-data exfiltration through prompts, uploads, plugins, connectors, and other AI interfaces.
Tune and validate AI-specific DLP and detection controls to ensure they operate effectively and identify relevant security risks.
Monitor developer-facing AI tools for policy compliance, credential exposure, non-human identity risks, and other security concerns.
Partner with engineering teams to establish and maintain appropriate security guardrails for code-assistance and agentic development tools.
Maintain and validate AI activity logging, retention, and audit controls to ensure sufficient visibility and traceability.
Collect, organise, and maintain evidence supporting AI security audits, ISO 42001 certification activities, AI impact assessments, and regulatory readiness initiatives.
Analyse false-positive and false-negative trends and recommend improvements to detection thresholds, rules, and investigation logic.
Identify recurring security patterns and contribute them to automation and security-response playbooks.
Collaborate with Security Operations, Identity, Legal, AI/ML Engineering, and governance stakeholders to align findings with incident response and risk-management processes.
Translate technical security findings into clear, risk-based narratives for governance forums, leadership, and executive reporting.

Requirements

3–5+ years of experience in security analysis, SOC, GRC, or a closely related cybersecurity role.
Working knowledge of SIEM platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or Google Chronicle, as well as DLP and CASB technologies.
Understanding of AI and LLM security risks, including prompt injection, AI-enabled data exfiltration, model or agent misuse, and shadow AI.
Familiarity with non-human identity concepts, including service accounts, API keys, OAuth tokens, and their associated security risks.
Understanding of threat detection methodologies and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK; exposure to MITRE ATLAS or the OWASP LLM Top 10 is strongly preferred.
Ability to interpret security logs, API telemetry, and structured or unstructured investigation data.
Basic scripting or query skills in Python, SQL, SPL, KQL, or comparable technologies for security investigations and reporting.
Strong written documentation skills and the ability to communicate complex technical findings through clear, risk-based narratives.
Familiarity with cloud environments such as AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Demonstrated, hands-on AI security experience in at least one relevant area, such as AI/LLM risk testing, prompt-injection investigation, AI-specific data-exfiltration analysis, shadow AI discovery, CASB/SWG-based application discovery, non-human identity investigations, or agentic AI/MCP security.
Practical experience should include a specific example of identifying a security issue, investigating its underlying cause, and contributing to an outcome or remediation.
Exposure to agentic AI or MCP-based architectures from either a security or engineering perspective is valuable, including experience with technologies such as LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, or MCP servers.
Hands-on exposure to AI governance frameworks such as ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, or EU AI Act risk classifications is advantageous, particularly through audit evidence collection or control testing.
Experience with security platforms such as Netskope, Zscaler, Wiz, Orca Security, Microsoft Purview, Abnormal Security, Bolster AI, or comparable technologies is a plus.
Exposure to ML-based anomaly detection or NLP-driven log analysis is beneficial.
Security certifications such as Security+, CISSP Associate, or relevant AI/ML security credentials are advantageous.
Strong analytical, investigative, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Benefits

Remote working opportunity from India.
Opportunity to work at the intersection of cybersecurity, AI, governance, and emerging technology.
Exposure to enterprise-scale AI security, threat detection, data protection, and identity-security challenges.
Collaboration with multidisciplinary teams spanning security operations, engineering, identity, legal, automation, and governance.
Opportunities to contribute to AI governance and compliance initiatives, including ISO 42001 and emerging AI regulatory requirements.
Professional growth through hands-on work with evolving AI security technologies, frameworks, and attack patterns.
Inclusive and collaborative working environment.

The Finance Program Manager provides strategic financial leadership, oversight, and business partnering across World Renew's Humanitarian & Emergency Affairs (HEA) portfolio, with primary responsibility for International Disaster Response (IDR) and additional support to Disaster Response Services (DRS) and Refugee Sponsorship & Resettlement Programs (RSRP).

The position serves as the primary finance focal point for HEA, ensuring sound financial stewardship, donor compliance, internal controls, financial monitoring, risk management, partner capacity strengthening, and effective financial management throughout the project lifecycle.

Working closely with the Director of Finance, the Head of Humanitarian & Emergency Affairs, country offices, implementing partners, and institutional donors, the Finance Program Manager provides strategic financial analysis and guidance that supports informed decision-making, strengthens financial accountability, mitigates risk, and promotes effective stewardship of humanitarian resources.

The position has primary responsibility for financial oversight of World Renew's Canadian Foodgrains Bank (CFGB) portfolio while also supporting institutional grants, humanitarian appeals, consortium awards, emergency response funding, and future donor-funded initiatives across the HEA portfolio.

As the principal financial liaison between the Finance Department and HEA, the position strengthens financial systems, improves internal controls, supports organizational learning, and promotes continuous improvement in humanitarian financial management across World Renew.

We do not discriminate based on disability, culture, ethnicity, or gender, and welcome and encourage people from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Major Duties And Responsibilities

Portfolio Financial Management & Oversight (30%)

Provide strategic financial management and oversight across the Humanitarian & Emergency Affairs portfolio, with primary responsibility for International Disaster Response.
Monitor portfolio financial performance, expenditure trends, forecasts, burn rates, budget utilization, and funding gaps.
Develop and maintain executive financial dashboards that provide timely analysis of portfolio performance, donor balances, appeal funding, foreign exchange exposure, and financial risks.
Prepare monthly portfolio financial reports, analysis, and recommendations for the Head of Humanitarian & Emergency Affairs, including emerging risks and actions to strengthen portfolio performance and financial stewardship.
Support annual budgeting, financial forecasting, and long-term portfolio planning.
Collaborate with finance and program teams to develop, monitor, and analyze cost recovery budgets and strategies across the HEA portfolio, maximizing recovery of direct and indirect costs while ensuring compliance with donor requirements.
Monitor humanitarian appeal funding, restricted and unrestricted balances, and funding utilization.
Coordinate fund transfers across the HEA portfolio with Finance and monitor project cash flow requirements.
Monitor exchange rate fluctuations and assess their impact on project budgets and portfolio performance.

Donor Financial Management & Compliance (15%)

Serve as the primary financial focal point for institutional donor-funded grants across the HEA portfolio.
Lead financial oversight of the Canadian Foodgrains Bank (CFGB) portfolio, including equity allocations, budget monitoring, donor compliance, financial reporting, and financial assurance activities.
Support financial management of consortium awards, humanitarian appeals, emergency response funding, and other institutional grants.
Review budget amendments, reallocations, financial reports, grant modifications, donor financial reviews, and grant closeout activities.
Lead development and review of proposal budgets, cost narratives, and supporting financial documentation for institutional funding opportunities.
Ensure compliance with donor regulations, funding agreements, and World Renew financial policies.
Support implementation of organizational sanctions screening, anti-terrorism measures, and other financial compliance requirements associated with institutional donor funding.
Coordinate responses to donor financial inquiries and financial monitoring requests.
Support post-award financial management throughout the project lifecycle.

Financial Monitoring, Internal Controls & Risk Management (25%)

Conduct targeted remote and in-person financial monitoring reviews, in coordination with country finance teams and implementing partners, to complement routine financial oversight, strengthen internal controls, and support donor compliance.
Perform periodic financial spot-checks of institutional donor-funded projects.
Review partner financial reports, supporting documentation, reconciliations, and financial management systems.
Assess financial risks and recommend practical mitigation measures.
Strengthen internal controls, segregation of duties, and financial assurance processes.
Monitor implementation of corrective action plans arising from financial reviews, audits, or donor monitoring visits.
Support fraud prevention initiatives and promote sound financial governance.
Coordinate and support external project audits and follow-up on audit recommendations.

Capacity Strengthening & Technical Support (15%)

Identify financial management capacity gaps and, as appropriate, develop, implement, and/or support capacity strengthening plans and learning opportunities for country offices and implementing partners
Provide technical guidance on financial management and compliance topics, including budgeting, financial reporting, donor requirements, grant financial management, and risk-informed decision-making.
Provide technical guidance and learning support to finance staff and program teams on donor financial requirements and organizational financial policies.
Promote localization by strengthening partner financial management systems and practices.

Financial Coordination & Organizational Support (10%)

Serve as the principal financial liaison between HEA and the Finance Department.
Support financial reporting processes by preparing and providing financial reports and analysis needed by program and leadership teams for program management, oversight, and decision-making.
Collaborate with program teams and procurement staff to support procurement planning, review procurement-related documentation, and ensure compliance with organizational procurement policies and donor requirements.
Support organizational financial planning and portfolio management discussions.
Collaborate with Grants, Program Management, and MEAL teams to strengthen project performance and financial accountability.
Promote sound stewardship by ensuring financial decisions align with donor expectations, organizational values, and program priorities.
Support cross-functional coordination on financial policies, procedures, templates, and organizational systems when they affect HEA financial management.

Strategic Finance & Continuous Improvement (5%)

Contribute to strategic financial planning across the HEA portfolio.
Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, reporting processes, templates, automation, and operational efficiency across the HEA portfolio.
Support organizational learning and continuous improvement by documenting financial lessons learned and applying best practices to future humanitarian financial management.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None

Qualifications

Personal Attributes

Demonstrates a personal Christian faith and commitment to the mission, vision, and values of World Renew.
Supports and contributes to an organizational culture rooted in Christian faith, service, justice, compassion, stewardship, and respect.
Demonstrates integrity, professionalism, sound judgment, and ethical financial stewardship.
Strong collaborative team player with the ability to work effectively across departments, cultures, and stakeholder groups.
Demonstrates initiative, flexibility, resilience, and adaptability in a dynamic humanitarian environment.
Strong analytical thinking, critical reasoning, and problem-solving abilities.
Excellent organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

Demonstrated expertise in financial management of institutional donor-funded humanitarian or international development programs.
Strong knowledge of donor financial compliance requirements, including budgeting, financial reporting, cost eligibility, and grant lifecycle management.

Description

Amazon's Transportation Operations Management (TOM) Central Programs org is driving change in the Middle Mile. The TOM PMO & Analytics team is looking for a Data Analyst to work within the Analytic Insights team to help drive data-driven decision-making, measurement, and reporting across TOM operations. In this role, you would be responsible for building, maintaining, and optimizing dashboards, metrics, and analytical solutions that support operational improvements and stakeholder needs across the organization. The TOM PMO & Analytics team delivers best-in-class centralized management of metrics, reporting, data quality, and analytical insights to drive TOM in-yard operational improvements across the Middle Mile.

Key job responsibilities

Design, build, and maintain dashboards and reports using Amazon QuickSight and other BI tools to support TOM operational metrics and leadership reporting
Analyze large-scale transportation operations datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and opportunities for operational improvement
Partner with program managers and operational stakeholders to define KPIs, establish measurement frameworks, and ensure consistent metric accountability
Develop and automate data pipelines, ETL processes, and reporting workflows to improve data accuracy and reduce manual effort
Implement and maintain AI-powered tools and automation to streamline data intake triage, stakeholder reporting, and operational analytics
Perform root cause analysis on metric variances and present findings with actionable recommendations to leadership
Ensure data integrity and quality across TOM dashboards by defining and enforcing data standards and validation processes
Support Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs) and other leadership mechanisms by preparing data-driven insights and variance callouts
Collaborate cross-functionally with various teams to translate business requirements into analytical solutions
Create and maintain documentation for data sources, metric definitions, data lineage, and standard operating procedures

About The Team

The TOM Program & Data Analytics team integrates strategic program management with analytics transformation across three pillars: 1. Program Execution — Drives end-to-end ownership of metric improvement, product development, and CPI initiatives from concept to measurable impact. 2. Change Management & Strategic Communication — Governs review, approval, and adoption of changes to standard work, policy, pilots, and proposals while aligning stakeholders through strategic communications. 3. Data & Analytics Insights — Ensures teams operate from accurate, timely metrics to identify gaps, measure progress, and make data-informed decisions. Together, these pillars enable TOM to execute programs, govern change, and run the business with data.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Knowledge of a modern programming language (Ruby, Java, Python, or C#)
Experience using data to drive root cause elimination and process improvement
Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements

Experience with Asana Project Management Platform, or proven experience with a similar intake and project management tool
Experience in transportation or supply chain
Experience in creating process improvements with automation and analysis, or experience working with Excel, reporting tools, and large-scale data mining tools, such as Power BI, Python, SQL, or Tableau

Description

The Leidos National Airspace Systems Integration Support (NISC) Program
is looking for a Program Analyst
to support the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) Office of Advanced Aviation Technologies (AAT).

The Office of Advanced Aviation Technologies will be the designated point for activities related to the integration of advanced aviation technologies including Advance Air Mobility, Unmanned Aircraft Systems, and Supersonic aircraft in United States.

In this role, the analyst will bridge the gap between technical data systems and day-to-day business needs. Core duties include leading the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) clearance process, improving data intake forms, managing datasets, and building dashboards / visualizations (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Power Apps, Tableau) to help leadership measure program performance.

Develop, monitor, and maintain a centralized Program KPI Framework, establishing baseline metrics, target thresholds, and automated reporting routines for leadership.
Query distributed data environments using advanced SQL to synthesize disparate data sources (e.g., using Starburst Trino across data lakehouses).
Design, deploy, and maintain executive-level data dashboards and advanced spreadsheet or financial models to visualize LOB activity, KPI trends, and program performance metrics (e.g., using Microsoft Excel, Tableau, or Power BI).
Oversee core program datasets to ensure high standards of accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and structural integrity.

Serve as the functional subject matter expert on program datasets, responding to ad-hoc data inquiries and audit calls from leadership and oversight entities.

Advanced proficiency and working knowledge of Power BI, Tableau, and PowerApps as well as SQL.

We’re looking for a Data Analyst to help drive better business decisions through thoughtful analysis, clear metric definitions, and strong cross-functional partnership. This role combines business-impact analytics with hands-on analytical data modeling. You’ll help build and maintain clean, reliable data models and transformations that support scalable reporting, trustworthy metrics, and informed decision-making. You’ll join a small, high-impact data team where ownership is meaningful and your work directly influences company growth.

## Key Responsibilities

* Partner cross-functionally to define KPIs, answer strategic questions, and support business decision-making.

## Required Qualifications

* 2–4 years of professional experience in a Data Analyst, Analytics Engineer, or similar analytics role.

* Experience performing exploratory analysis and translating findings into actionable business insights.

* Experience driving measurable business impact through analytics.
* Experience building analytical data models, not only dashboards and ad hoc reports.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to explain complex datasets, analysis, and technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
* Proactive mindset with willingness to take ownership of projects and work outside your immediate area of expertise.
* Familiarity with data ingestion tools such as Fivetran, Airbyte, Stitch, or similar platforms.
* Familiarity with dbt, SQLMesh, Dataform, or similar data transformation tools.
* Familiarity with modern BI tools such as Tableau, Sigma, Looker, or similar platforms.
* Familiarity with version-controlled analytics workflows.
* Understanding of dimensional modeling concepts, including fact tables, dimension tables, and star schemas.
* Proficiency in SQL is required.
* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or another related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Demonstrated experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, or other business stakeholders.

## Preferred Qualifications

* Experience building predictive or inference models.
* Experience building and maintaining data ingestion pipelines.
* Experience implementing data quality testing and documentation practices.
* Experience working with GTM teams to define and report on GTM metrics.
* Exposure to event-based or product analytics data.
* Experience using AI effectively as part of an analytics workflow.
* Experience with modern analytics tooling and cloud data platforms.
* Experience contributing to forecasting, experimentation, or advanced analytical initiatives.

The current analytics environment includes:

* Airbyte
* BigQuery
* SQLMesh

Job Posting:

Since 1953, Ferguson has been a source of quality supplies for a variety of industries. Together We Build Better infrastructure, better homes and better businesses. We exist to make our customers’ complex projects simple, successful, and sustainable. We proactively solve problems, adapt and grow to continuously serve our customers, communities and each other. Ferguson, a Fortune 500 company, is proud to provide best-in-class products, service and capabilities across the following industries: Commercial/Mechanical, Facilities Supply, Fire and Fabrication, HVAC, Industrial, Residential Trade, Residential Building and Remodel, Waterworks and Residential Digital Commerce. Ferguson has approximately 36,000 associates across 1,700 locations. Ferguson is a community of proud associates who operate with the shared purpose of building something meaningful. You will build a career that you are proud of, at a company you can believe in.

Enterprise PMO Program Manager

We are seeking an associate to join the Enterprise Strategy & Planning team to oversee the alignment and execution of approved critical initiatives & programs. The Enterprise Strategy & Planning team enables strategy development and resource alignment to support strategy execution. The team provides leadership and capabilities around strategic planning & development, program & project management, business planning, and corporate venture.

As Enterprise PMO Program Manager, you will be responsible for effective and efficient planning and execution of the initiatives to deliver results on time, on budget.

This position will require engagement with Vice Presidents and Directors leading critical initiatives and transparent communication will be key. A high degree of business acumen, ability to collaborate and influence all personality types, and efficient facilitation is key.

This position is a hybrid role in Newport News, VA. (Schedule 3 days in office, usually T, W, Th and 2 days Remote usually M, F). More office time may be needed for onboarding, training or meetings.

We may consider a Remote for the right individual who lives outside the Newport News area.

Responsibilities:

Program Leadership: Lead the end-to-end management of strategic programs. Act as a strategic thought partner.
Cross-Functional Orchestration: Drive alignment and commonality across customer groups, business, functions (e.g., Technology, HR, Finance etc) and other key partner groups to ensure seamless program execution and effective communication.
Planning & Execution: Develop and implement comprehensive program plans, proactively manage dependencies and risks, and ensure adherence to budgetary and resource allocation parameters.
Outcome-Driven Management: Define and monitor key performance indicators to ensure programs achieve intended business outcomes, with a focus on value realization and return on investment.
Program Management Excellence: Mentor and guide project/ program management personnel, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence within the organization.

Drives Accountability: A strong natural leadership style that motivates and inspires excellence and drives high standards for individual, team, and organizational accomplishment through teamwork and empowerment; tenaciously work to meet or exceed challenging goals and foster continuous improvement.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Project Management, or a related field.

Experience:
7+ years’ experience with project management
5+ years’ experience functional experience in implementing process changes and running large, complex projects
5+ years of experience in large-scale Programs/Projects
Experience across multiple project types including technology and non-technology projects

Able to drive decision making across all levels of the organization, across multi-disciplined and matrixed teams

new_jobs.title: Tech Infra Program Manager, DC Power Utilization Management
new_jobs.description:
Description

About the Role

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager (TIPM) to join the Power & Utilization Management and Planning (PUMP) team within AWS Infrastructure Services. This role is responsible for driving programs that maximize power capacity, improve position planning accuracy, and accelerate rack deployment across AWS's global fleet of data centers.

What You'll Do

As a TIPM on the PUMP team, you will own sub-workstreams within one or more of the following program areas, working under the guidance of senior TIPMs who hold end-to-end accountability. You will drive execution on defined scopes, remove blockers, coordinate across partner teams, and progressively take on broader ownership as you build domain expertise.

Data Center Position Configuration & Automation

The Soapstone workflow produces three interdependent datasets per build — rack placement on the floor plan, power circuit-to-rack mapping (which determines what whips get physically installed), and network cabling plans (which determine how server racks connect to aggregation racks). These outputs determine what gets physically built: general contractors install whips from them, electrical engineers configure three-phase power equipment at the rack level, and mechanical engineers reference them for downstream work. When this workflow is delayed or incorrect, construction stalls, hardware ships to positions that cannot support it, and capacity delivery slips. You will own sub-workstreams within this pipeline — for example, driving configuration for a set of availability zones, managing the intake and validation process through SLATE (the team's build coordination portal), or accelerating Hamlet automation coverage to new building classes (COLO sites, hybrid floor plans, Room 1 configurations).

Power Reclamation & Infrastructure Upgrades

You will drive specific remediation campaigns that recover stranded power across legacy data centers through electrical upgrades, PDC (Power Distribution Cabinet) deployments, cooling improvements, and breaker-level optimizations. The power distribution landscape is complex: four distinct PDC versions are active in the fleet with different breaker counts and ampacity ratings, whip counts range from 18 to 26 per rack depending on product type, and whip lengths are tracked manually in Excel files rather than any system of record. You will coordinate across Field Remediation Engineering (FRE), Construction Project Implementation (CPI), Colocation Regional Engineering (CRE), and equipment procurement teams to execute physical infrastructure changes on time.

Network & Server Position Planning

You will own sub-workstreams that improve how network and server positions are planned, allocated, and made ready for deployment. A key challenge is that every rack product connects to the network differently — connection protocols vary (RoCE vs. EFA), server-to-switch ratios vary (3:1, 2:1, 1:1), and switch rack generations keep evolving (12.8T, 51.2T, 102.4T Ultra). You will work with Fulfillment Planning (FP), Capacity Delivery Planning (CDP), and Global Network Deployment (GND) on initiatives like the Fungible Network program, which deploys a standard product-agnostic network footprint per ROMP so that product flips no longer require cabling rework. You will use and improve tools like RATS and PRP to increase allocation rates and reduce rejection rates at scale.

Power Data Modeling & Metrics

You will contribute to the development and maintenance of power-related data models, dashboards, and sources of truth that inform executive-level decisions on capacity investment, utilization targets, and demand planning. This includes working with data engineering and BI teams to build QuickSight dashboards, validate Power SOT (Source of Truth) data, and support Monthly and Weekly Business Reviews.

Utility Power Management

You will support programs that optimize utility power utilization to meet contractual obligations and avoid financial penalties. This includes monitoring site-level deployed load against contracted capacity, identifying sites at risk of under-utilization, and coordinating with energy and operations teams to improve utilization rates.

Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

You will work daily with 10+ partner organizations including CDP, CRE, CPI, FRE, DCEO, GND, Hardware Engineering, ML Planning, AISS Science, and Networking. Success in this role requires the ability to influence without authority, drive accountability across organizational boundaries, and escalate effectively when blockers arise.

About The Team

The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management
Experience working with data and leveraging analytics to make decisions
Experience communicating and handling cross-functional programs including project stakeholders, technical program managers, and software development teams

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in data center, networking engineering, systems engineering or construction management with a good understanding of data center technologies such as power, cooling and controls systems
Experience with Tableau, Python, SQB, Quicksight, Cognos or or other BI packages
Knowledge of electrical engineering principles including switchgear, UPS, transformers, and circuit breakers
Experience with statistical analytics and programming languages such as R, Python, Ruby, etc.

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. The PUMP team sits at the intersection of data center engineering, supply chain operations, and capacity planning. We own the end-to-end lifecycle of how power is planned, configured, allocated, and utilized across thousands of lineups, hundreds of data centers, and dozens of clusters worldwide. Our decisions directly impact AWS's ability to deliver compute, storage, and machine learning capacity to customers — from core EC2 workloads to the latest GPU-accelerated ML platforms like GB300, VR200, and TRN3Max.

Experience in project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management

Description

Build the proof that convinces customers to move to AWS. As a Benchmarking Program Manager, you will create and evangelize new benchmarking studies that quantify the KPI-driven benefits customers can achieve on AWS — the credible, data-backed evidence that AWS field teams and customers rely on to build the business case for cloud. You own these studies end to end, and once they scale, your work becomes the standard the field sells on. This is a rare seat with real autonomy: you will own the full study lifecycle, including the external vendor relationship, and you will shape how cloud value is measured and communicated across internal and external audiences. You will partner across teams to understand the needs of internal and external users, develop plans to scale each study's impact, and find innovative ways to apply benchmark insights to value-based business cases for cloud adoption. If you are energized by turning complex economics into clear, compelling proof points, move fluidly between analytical rigor and go-to-market storytelling, and thrive owning a program from concept through launch and scale, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities

Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to design studies and communicate the market realities of running IT applications and infrastructure in the cloud versus a traditional data center.
Develop and conduct new benchmarking studies that help customers understand the financial and operational benefits of the cloud.
Own the entire benchmarking study process and the external vendor relationship, including creating RFPs and evaluating, selecting, and managing vendors.
Develop and execute go-to-market and scaling mechanisms that put new studies in front of the field and customers.
Design and manage program impact-tracking metrics for management reporting.

A day in the life

You might start the morning reviewing preliminary data from a vendor-led benchmarking study, then jump into a working session with AWS field teams to understand which customer pain points the next study should address. After lunch you could be drafting the go-to-market narrative for a recently completed study, collaborating with marketing and sales enablement to ensure the messaging resonates. Later, you will connect with an external research vendor to align on methodology and timelines, and close out the day by updating your program dashboard so leadership has a clear view of study pipeline and impact.

About The Team

The AWS Cloud Economics Scale team builds tools, intellectual property, and methodology to help customers identify and quantify value creation opportunities at each stage of their journey to the cloud. We engage directly and collaboratively with customers and internal AWS teams to deliver cloud value expertise. The Cloud Economics Scale team helps answer the question: "What value can I expect to achieve by using AWS?"

3+ years of program or project management experience

Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Knowledge of Microsoft Excel (macros, pivots, lookups) at an advanced level

With over 50 years of proven success, ECG, ranked as a Best Midsized Firm to Work For 2026 by Consulting Magazine , is the most experienced healthcare consulting firm in the US. Working exclusively in this space, our people consistently demonstrate their ability to solve challenges for providers and achieve better patient outcomes. Across our seven office locations, we’re seeking individuals who will show the courage to find innovative solutions and make a direct impact on the delivery of healthcare services nationwide.

About ECG

ECG is a national consulting firm that is redefining healthcare together with its clients. We provide a broad range of strategic, financial, operational, and technology-enabled consulting services to the full continuum of care, including hospitals, health systems, medical groups, academic medical centers, children’s hospitals, cancer centers, ambulatory surgery centers, investors, and payers/health plans.

Our work focuses on creating practical, tailored solutions that help clients maximize resources and achieve sustainable results. We value collaboration, integrity, and innovation, and are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive work environment.

Job Details

Join Our Analytics Hub

Our growing Analytics Hub works with our consulting teams to deliver new insights, streamlined analysis, and world-class intelligence to the healthcare organizations we serve as clients. Combined with our consulting teams, you will be helping physician and executive leadership make informed decisions that can alter the course of their enterprises in areas such as physician alignment, mergers and acquisitions, service line planning, provider compensation, financial performance, transforming care models, patient access, managed care portfolio optimization, digital health expansion, and more. ECG uses a Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365 environment, with Microsoft Power BI as ECG’s current analytics visualization platform.

Our detailed plans incorporate qualitative findings with data-driven strategic, operational, and financial considerations that enable organizations to pursue realistic change. Our consultants bridge the gap between strategic thinking and operational implementation with sensible action plans and tactical recommendations. This approach allows us to stretch our clients’ thinking while ensuring that initiatives with the broadest and deepest impact are prioritized and implementable. Our wide-ranging engagements often focus on helping our clients:

Position themselves for value-based care delivery.
Align hospitals and physician organizations.
Strengthen financial performance.
Enhance clinical programs.
Develop strategic partnerships and/or mergers.

As a senior data analyst, you will support the firm’s client delivery and business development efforts, working with consultants and senior leaders to manage large datasets, aggregate internal and external data, develop scalable models and other analyses, and support data visualization and presentation sets. In addition, the analyst will work directly with our internal support teams (IT, business development, and L&D) and associated vendors for data management and IT solutions and will assist with a range of innovative analytic opportunities. Gather and synthesize data from various sources (e.g., national surveys, proprietary research, client interviews, industries, markets).

Communicate market insights to pursuit teams, and support business development efforts.
Configure, maintain, and build flexible reports, queries, and visuals within the Power BI environment and the production and development environments of related databases.
Research, test, and implement solutions in Power BI.
Partner with various consulting units (Strategy & Enterprise Growth, Payer Strategy & Contracting, Health System Performance, and Medical Group Optimization) to gather requirements related to data analytics.
Develop, configure, and maintain interfaces to exchange data among Power BI, SQL databases, and other cloud-based applications.
Create and maintain analytical support documentation and operating procedures.
Develop new and innovative methodologies and approaches.
Contribute to internal education and learning opportunities for consultants and operations members for the Analytics Hub and analytics in general, and support education about ECG’s use cases related to analytics.
Assist the vice president of data analytics and AI in developing analytics and data strategy to support data analytics capabilities at the firm.

A bachelor’s degree in either computer science, computer engineering, mathematics, statistics, health information management, or a related degree that relies heavily on critical thinking, logic, and math
5+ years of experience in healthcare data analytics, including analyzing clinical, operational, financial, or population health data
Experience in healthcare consulting, healthcare technology, or working for a hospital or health system, using data to deliver actionable insights and recommendations
Strong proficiency in data analysis, reporting, dashboard development, and translating complex data into actionable business insights
Experience working with healthcare datasets such as claims, EHRs, patient outcomes, quality metrics, or value-based care programs is highly preferred
Advanced skills in SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI); experience with Python, R, Databricks, or Azure is a plus

Strong written and verbal communication skills
Excellent organizational skills

Here at innocent, we’re on a mission to make it easier for everyone to get more fruit and veg into their bodies. We started back in 1999 and since then we’ve gone from selling a few smoothies at a music festival to becoming one of Europe’s biggest drinks companies with around 1,000 people (and the B Corp seal of approval).

It’s nice to be able to say things like that but we’re not patting ourselves on the back just yet. We want to show everyone that it’s possible to be a successful business while looking after people and the planet too, so we’re trying to get better in pretty much every way. And that’s where this job comes in.

This advert is for our Project Management talent pool. There isn’t an open role right now, but we regularly hire Project Managers at different levels and want to meet great people before we need them.

If a suitable role comes up, we’ll be in touch.

What You’ll Be Doing (depending On The Role)

The exact responsibilities will vary by role and level. That said, Project Managers at innocent typically get involved in things like:

Managing projects from idea to delivery (and occasionally celebration)
Creating clear plans, timelines and ways of working
Coordinating cross‑functional teams across marketing, supply chain, tech, finance and beyond
Tracking progress, risks, dependencies and budgets
Helping teams stay focused when priorities shift
Communicating updates in a way that makes sense to humans
Improving how we do project delivery over time

Senior Roles May Also Include

Leading complex programmes or multiple projects at once
Influencing senior stakeholders and decision‑making
Coaching or mentoring more junior Project Managers

Entry‑level Roles May Focus More On

Supporting project delivery and governance
Learning project tools, methodologies and best practice
Building confidence working with stakeholders

You’ll need

Again, this will vary depending on the role, but we’re generally looking for people who:

Enjoy organising work and bringing clarity to complexity
Communicate clearly, openly and with empathy
Are comfortable working with different teams and viewpoints
Can balance detail with the bigger picture
Take ownership and follow things through

For More Senior Roles, We’ll Also Look For

Proven experience delivering projects end‑to‑end
Confidence managing risk, ambiguity and change
Strong stakeholder management skills

What You’ll Get

A role matched to your experience, whether you’re building your foundations in project delivery or leading complex initiatives
The chance to work on meaningful, cross‑functional projects from idea through to delivery
Clear expectations around ownership, accountability and ways of working
Exposure to different teams, disciplines and stakeholders across the organisation
Opportunities to develop your project management skills, confidence and impact over time
The space to improve how projects are run, not just deliver them
Senior roles typically come with broader influence, more complexity, and responsibility for shaping delivery approaches. Entry‑level roles focus more on learning, support and building strong project fundamentals.

Good To Know

This is a Talent Pool and not tied to a current vacancy. We’ll review applications as we build our pipeline and reach out when a relevant opportunity comes up.

We want innocent to be a great place to work, so we do lots of stuff to make people feel at home and try to make sure everyone’s career is shaping up the way they want it to. There are plenty of opportunities to have a go at something new or take things further.

In exchange for helping us do business in the right way, you’ll get a solid rewards package that includes a salary (phew), private healthcare, a target-based bonus, and a bunch of other nice things like a day off on your birthday. And yes, you get free smoothies.

We also know that not all our drinkers come from the same background, or think the same – so why should we? At innocent, we want to be a great place to work where a diverse bunch of people from all backgrounds can turn up and thrive. When we hire, we want all the juice, bits, and pulp that make you who you are.

Even if you don’t think you can tick all the boxes, if the job sounds right for you, come and throw your hat in the ring.

Overview

The Senior Project Manager is responsible for all project administration including all contractual requirements, agreements with trade partners, purchase orders, and risk management. This individual also manages general work performance and quality, and overall team progress against the project plan.

Suffolk is seeking people who are bold. Curious. Innovative. Caring. Looking for the career opportunity of a lifetime. We’ll challenge and inspire you to be your very best. We’ll embrace what makes you unique and lift you up as you take chances. Here, you’ll find a place where you can act with purpose and integrity, bringing intelligence and grit to every aspect of your job. Join us for the chance to achieve your ambitions and build your legacy.

Responsibilities

Budget Updates:
Produce thorough forecast of Cost-to-Complete which drills down to identify potential exposures
Coordinate the use of Oracle with Expedition to readily identify exposures
Require the project team to track costs of field directives and back charges for forecasting purposes
Create detailed analysis of line-item exposures, particularly unit price contracts
Follow the Forecasting Calendar for on-time completion of forecasts
Teach the Standard Operating Procedures for budget updating to others
Change Order Management:
Require the project team to fully utilize Expedition to track all Proposed Change Order (PCO) items including in-scope and out-of-scope
Provide the Owner with up-to-date status reports relating to Changes
Require the project team to produce a monthly Owner Change Order (OCO) to prevent aging of PCO issues which further allows for timely closure of Changes with Subcontractors
Work to recover all legitimate GC costs relating to Owner Changes
Track the status of all Contract Allowances in Expedition and submits Change Order Requests (COR) when an over-run is likely
Require the project team to track all field directives and back charges in Expedition for timely processing on a monthly basis, i.e. composite clean-up, hoisting time, etc.
Project Close Out:
Establish an effective Close-out Plan early in the project which includes the early collection, review, and packaging of Contract close-out documents
Implement the use of the Noncompliance Reporting System
Require the team to utilize the Work list System to organize and manage the completion of phases of the work
Utilize the Completion-Compliance-Quality Form (CCQ) process for close-out
Teach close out process to other SCCI employees
Owner/Sub Requisition Process:
Require the project team to have the completed pay requisitions approved by the Owner no later than the 1st of each month
Produce an effective Schedule of Values
Establish a regimented process for the collection of payments no later than 30 days and subsequent efficient system for the payment to Subcontractors
Review the Hold Reports before payment is due to allow for timely handling of deficiency issues and payment to Subcontractors/Vendors
Cash Management:
Consistently manage the cash flow of the Project to maintain a fiscally responsible position for SCCI
Produce an effective Schedule of Values which supports a strong cash flow position
Review each Subcontractors initial Schedule of Values to prevent overpayment
Review Sub/Vendor requisitions to prevent payment of unsigned or unfunded Change Orders
Produce and update the cash model for the Owner to prevent surprises
Produce an accurate percent complete projection to support the SCCI financial management process
Meeting Management:
Establishes a meeting regiment for the Project Team which provides for effective communication and problem solving
Follow the SOP for focused meetings such as PM/PE, OAC's, subcontractor meetings, coordination meetings, Precon Sessions, etc.
Manage all meetings by agenda and work to time limits
Contract Logs:
Require the Project Team to assemble and maintain the Project Logs (Cash Management, Change Management, Noncompliance, Buy-Schedule, Contracts, Procurement, Submittals, RFI's, Safety, Hold Reports, Construction Schedule, Work lists) and periodically review for accuracy
Conduct focus meetings once per month to review the maintenance of those logs and drills down to identify potential exposures and issues
Subcontractor Relationships:
Establish a "Firm but Fair" approach to building relationships with Subcontractors
Promote an environment of organization and professionalism with Subcontractors
Address issues immediately with a non-performing Subcontractor to protect SCCI from resulting delay and potential impact
Exhibit B Purchasing Process:
Work with the Project Team, including Superintendents and Estimators, to consistently produce clear, thorough, and accurate Scopes of Work based on drilled down review of documents
Organize and administer a well-planned purchasing process to prevent the "Just in time" purchase of materials
Understand the priority of timely buy-out and gather the resources to meet the buy schedule
Schedule Management:
Provide leadership with the Superintendent to produce a clear, thorough, and accurate baseline Contract Schedule which rarely requires changes to the original logic
Track events, impacts, and changes in the schedule to allow for the management and prevention of delays
Lead the Project Team to focus on critical path matters to prevent non-excusable delays
Manage and distribute organized and efficient Monthly Updating Process in accordance with the SCCI SOP
Provide the Owner with written monthly updates of the Contract Schedule in accordance with the requirements of the Contract
Take decisive action with subcontractors that are impacting the schedule
Produce buy-out and procurement schedule and assist with writing monthly schedule narrative in conjunction with the Scheduling team
Risk Management:
Complete the buy-out process in a manner which permits the timely flow of work, prevents budget issues, contract executions, bonds, insurance, etc.
Write timely notices to Owner and Subcontractors
Secure CCD authorizations before proceeding with Changes
Take immediate action when a non-performing Subcontractor is likely to cause impact to the Project
Work to complete the submittal and coordination process no later than 180 days
Teaches a risk management regiment to others on the project team
Owner Relationship:
Work to establish a trusting and professional relationship with the Owner
Focus on keeping the Owner well informed of important matters to prevent surprises
Work to secure a strong letter of recommendation from the Owner for SCCI
Quality Management:
Provide leadership in the utilization of the Quality Management Program on the project, which outlines quality expectations
Participate with the project team to institute the use of First Delivery and Quality Benchmark Inspections as the work progresses
Implement the use of the Nonconformance Reporting System to track and manage deficiencies in the work
Require the use of mock-ups to establish the quality expectations as defined in the Quality Management Program
Team Leadership:
Strive to create synergy and a teamwork atmosphere on the project
Lead by example by establishing the work ethic guidelines for the entire team and therefore establishes the boundaries and expectations
Organize periodic team events and training sessions to advance the SCCI strategy of "Train & Develop Our People
Act immediately when personal conflicts emerge among the team
Mentoring/Training:
Oversee career and educational development of team personnel
Require the adherence of standard operation procedures and actively teach each process

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in applicable discipline and a minimum of 10 years of experience relative to project size and scope
Excellent business judgment demonstrated by consistently achieving profitability objectives and strong project close-outs with client and subcontractor relationships in good standing
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail evidenced by a strong command of all applicable contract and legal provisions
Ability to consistently analyze and execute financial trade-offs which frequently involve dealing with incomplete data and ambiguity
Ability to constantly multi-task and handle competing priorities between Suffolk business needs, organizational issues, and sound customer relations
Possess judgment to know when to appropriately escalate issues up the chain of command
The ability to manage and embrace change. Respond and adapt to new processes and new ways of looking at old problems
A strong sense of urgency and initiative. Able to quickly study and react to complex issues
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to confidently and decisively take action
Team leader with excellent diplomatic and communication skills, able to handle and resolve conflicts effectively in a firm but fair manner
Candidate must possess Suffolk’s Core Values: Passion, Integrity, Hard Work, Professionalism, and Caring

Working Conditions

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for long periods of time; talk or hear; perform fine motor, hand and finger skills in the use of a keyboard, telephone, or writing. The employee is frequently required to stand; walk; and reach with arms and/or hands. Specific vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus. The employee will spend their time in an office environment with a quiet to moderate noise level. Job site walking.
